ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Approximately 75% high-intensity (white) pixels to 25% low-intensity (black) pixels across the visible ventral fluke area.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Dominant contiguous white fields occupy the center of both lobes. Low-intensity black pigmentation is mapped to the entire perimeter (leading and trailing edges) and forms a broad vertical pillar from the peduncle to the notch. Fine black mottling and 'splatter' patterns extend from the central pillar into the interior white fields.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep V-shaped depression with an approximate pixel angle of 62 degrees and a depth ratio of roughly 1:6 relative to total fluke height.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Continuous high-frequency serration along the trailing boundary. Serrations exhibit irregular pixel amplitudes ranging from 2-10 pixels, with the highest density of jagged peaks located on the distal half of both the left and right lobes.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Primary concave curve originating from the median notch, transitioning to a neutral/linear mid-section, and terminating in a convex distal sweep towards the tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: A dense cluster of high-contrast, circular white structures (approximately 8-10 units) is visible on the terminal edge of the right fluke tip, consistent with barnacle colonization.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Detection of 4-6 distinct, dark linear pixel streaks on the white surface of the left lobe, oriented vertically and sub-parallel to each other.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Ectoparasitic calcifications (barnacles) on the right distal tip; multiple small irregular nicks and non-uniform indentations along the trailing edge topography.
other_distinctive_markers: Highly unique dendritic black pigmentation pattern at the interface between the central dark axial region and the white lateral fields.
